falsifier.1_correctedDiagramDiffersFromDraft: SCORED PASS. Multiple elements differ from the draft, each verified at source, not merely re-asserted: (a) all 40 Cloud Run jobs and 4 services live in ONE GCP project, hauska-prod-497015, confirmed by `gcloud run jobs/services list`; (b) the atoms store and the landing store share one Neon PROJECT (cortex-prod / fancy-fire-06136146), confirmed by Neon API branch listing showing both 'neondb' and 'hauska_mcp' secrets resolve into the same project's branches; (c) 'staging' is already a reused Neon branch PAIR in that project (not a fresh-per-run branch), confirmed by Neon API operations log showing delete_timeline+create_branch resets under the same names on 2026-09-14; (d) the factory store has exactly ONE branch, ever, confirmed by Neon API branch listing (this directly corrects the draft's Option B description, which implies factory branching is a straightforward extension of an existing pattern -- it is not, for the factory-store half); (e) the factory store already has a read-replica endpoint, confirmed by Neon API endpoints listing plus two post-incident Secret Manager entries (FACTORY_DATABASE_URL_RO, FACTORY_DATABASE_URL_REPLICA), not shown in the draft's diagram; (f) PUBLISH_TARGETS/WRITER_TARGETS are frozen 2-value enums in both repos' code, confirmed by `git show` on origin/main -- absent from the draft entirely and the single most consequential correction; (g) 6 stray Neon branches from 2026-08-27/28 are confirmed still alive and, in several cases, still active TODAY (2026-09-16), upgrading the draft's 'branch cleanup, 2026-08-28' bullet from a historical incident to a live unresolved condition.
falsifier.2_optionSurvivesTwoCountiesOneHour: SCORED: RECOMMENDED OPTION SURVIVES, WITH A NAMED PRECONDITION, NOT UNCONDITIONALLY. Walked step by step in report Section 4 against publish-target-env.mjs / writer-target-env.mjs: the bookkeeping layer (publish_runs keyed by (county_fips, target), leases keyed by (entity_type, county_fips)) already tolerates two counties publishing in the same hour on shared stores TODAY, confirmed by schema. But two counties CANNOT each get their own isolated branch/compute under a distinct name today, because the target name is a frozen 2-value enum pointing at one fixed secret pair per name -- confirmed by code, not assumed. The recommended B+D architecture therefore survives the falsifier only once the target model is generalized beyond 2 values (named as precondition 1 in the report); as currently coded, two farms sharing the literal string 'staging' would be sharing one Neon branch pair, which is a real, code-confirmed limitation the draft did not have.
falsifier.3_everyCapacityNumberSourced: SCORED PASS, WITH EXPLICIT UNMEASURED MARKERS WHERE A NUMBER COULD NOT BE RE-SOURCED. All capacity-table entries in report Section 2 name their source (a specific Neon API path, a specific SQL query against a named table, or a gcloud command). Three figures are explicitly marked UNMEASURED / UNMEASURED-IN-SESSION rather than carried from memory: the Neon plan's branch-count ceiling (no read endpoint returned it), parcel-envelope-cells/parcel-setback-cells row throughput (zero counts/cost/run_events on all 14 sampled runs -- a finding in itself), and the draft's specific 67.4/149.0 atoms/s figure (not disputed, but not re-derivable from any table this session could read, since atoms_writer_lease_history carries no row-count column).

contradicted: The draft's Option B description ('a factory branch and an atoms branch per county, each with its own compute') implies a roughly symmetric extension of one existing pattern to both stores. Measured this session: the atoms/landing side already has a reused-in-place staging branch pair (an existing, if singular, pattern); the factory store has never been branched at all (zero prior art). Building 'a branch pair per farm' is therefore two different-sized jobs, not one job done twice. Separately, the draft's framing of the Bastrop-named publish job as the main county-literal risk undersold the real blocker: the job's CONTENTS are already fully county-generic (confirmed: TX_COUNTY_FIPS_SET has all 254 counties, and the job's own header comment states nothing inside assumes Bastrop) -- the frozen PUBLISH_TARGETS/WRITER_TARGETS enum, which the draft never mentions, is the actual structural constraint on running more than one farm concurrently.
